problem.title: Price per Notebook
problem.statement: Six identical notebooks cost $18 altogether. What is the cost per notebook?
hints: Per one notebook means divide the total dollars by six notebooks.

validationMethods: Independent multiplication check: 6 notebooks × $3/notebook = $18; only B reconstructs the stated total.

problem.title: Scale a Walking Rate
problem.statement: Mina walks 15 miles in 3 hours at a constant rate. How far does she walk in 7 hours?
hints: First find miles per one hour.

solutionSteps.title: Find and use the unit rate
solutionSteps.body: 15 miles ÷ 3 hours = 5 miles per hour. Then 5 miles/hour × 7 hours = 35 miles.

validationMethods: Independent proportion audit: 15/3 = x/7 gives 3x = 105 and x = 35; only C matches.
notes: The constant-rate condition licenses direct scaling.

problem.title: Minutes for 600 Words
problem.statement: A reader finishes 240 words in 4 minutes at a constant rate. How many minutes will 600 words take?
hints: Find words per minute, then divide words by words per minute.

solutionSteps.title: Track the units
solutionSteps.body: 240 words ÷ 4 minutes = 60 words/minute. Then 600 words ÷ 60 words/minute = 10 minutes.

validationMethods: Unit-chain method: 240/4 = 60 words/minute and 600/(60 words/minute) = 10 minutes.
Independent scale-factor check: 600/240 = 2.5, so time is 4×2.5 = 10 minutes; only C matches.
notes: The target asks for the inverse quantity, time rather than output.

problem.title: Miles per Gallon
problem.statement: A car travels 120 miles using 3 gallons of fuel. What is its average rate in miles per gallon?
hints: The phrase miles per gallon fixes the division order.

solutionSteps.title: Follow the requested unit
solutionSteps.body: Miles per gallon means miles divided by gallons: 120 ÷ 3 = 40 miles per gallon.

validationMethods: Requested-unit calculation: 120 miles/3 gallons = 40 miles per gallon.
Independent reconstruction: 40 miles/gallon × 3 gallons = 120 miles; only C reconstructs the trip.
notes: The wording makes per operational rather than decorative.

problem.title: Compare Two Cycling Rates
problem.statement: Cyclist A travels 150 miles in 3 hours. Cyclist B travels 224 miles in 4 hours. Who has the greater average speed, and by how many miles per hour?
problem.shortAnswer: Cyclist B by 6 miles per hour
hints: Normalize both trips to miles per one hour before comparing.

solutionSteps.title: Find both unit rates
solutionSteps.body: Cyclist A averages 150/3 = 50 miles per hour. Cyclist B averages 224/4 = 56 miles per hour.

solutionSteps.title: Compare like units
solutionSteps.body: 56 − 50 = 6, so Cyclist B is faster by 6 miles per hour.

validationMethods: Separate unit-rate computation: 150/3 = 50 mph and 224/4 = 56 mph; difference 6 mph favors B.
Independent common-time check: in 12 hours A would travel 600 miles and B 672 miles, a 72-mile difference over 12 hours, equivalent to 6 mph; only C matches.
notes: Both quantities are normalized to identical units before subtraction.
